title: Let checkout read exchange rates while the table reloads

blocks.text: Checkout prices every basket in euros through `RateTable`, which loads exchange rates from the rate store on first use and again after each `refresh()`. A full load takes a few seconds.

Two incidents shaped what is wanted. The first version held a lock while it loaded, and after every refresh the checkout threads queued behind the load: p99 latency jumped by four seconds. The fix for that answered some baskets with "no rate for NOK" for as long as a load was running.

items: `table()`: return the current table, loading it if there is none;
`load()`: one full load from the store.

blocks.text: When you're done, a lookup never waits for a load another thread started (two threads loading at the same time is acceptable, as both get the same rates), a lookup never sees a table that is missing rates the store has, and the map `rates()` hands to the end-of-day report can't be used to change the rates every other caller sees. About eight lines in total.
The tests hold the store in the middle of a load and make lookups from other threads meanwhile.

cases.says: lookups are answered from one load of the store until a refresh, after which the new rates are loaded
a lookup made while another thread's load is still running is answered without waiting for that load
a lookup made while another thread's load is still running sees every rate, never a partly loaded table
a caller that tries to change the rates it was handed changes nothing for other callers

origin.section: A Race Is Benign Only When Every Thread Writes the Same Value, in One Indivisible Write, Read Once

concepts: A cache may race only when every thread computes the same value from immutable input and stores it in one write that can't tear; a racy recomputation then costs only time.
A lazily cached mutable object is not a benign race: other threads can see it before it is complete, and a change made through it reaches every caller.
